A criterion for determinantal presentations of numerical semigroup rings

Satoshi Murai Address:  Satoshi Murai, Department of Mathematics Faculty of Education Waseda University, 1-6-1 Nishi-Waseda, Shinjuku, Tokyo 169-8050, Japan Email address: s-murai@waseda.jp and Kou Takahashi Address:  Kou Takahashi, Department of Mathematics Faculty of Education Waseda University, 1-6-1 Nishi-Waseda, Shinjuku, Tokyo 169-8050, Japan Email address: k_takahash@akane.waseda.jp
Abstract.

We study numerical semigroups whose defining ideals admit determinantal presentations by the 2×22\times 2 minors of a 2×n2\times n matrix. A conjecture of Cuong, Kien, Matsuoka, and Truong relates such presentations to arithmetic progressions of pseudo-Frobenius numbers. We prove a numerical criterion for this determinantal presentation, reducing the conjecture to a problem on factorizations of maximal elements of an Apéry set in the numerical semigroup. As an application, we verify the conjecture in embedding dimension four under a unique factorization assumption on an Apéry set.

1. Introduction

In this paper, we study numerical semigroups whose defining ideals are generated by the 2×22\times 2 minors of a 2×n2\times n matrix. We begin by recalling some basic notation and background; we refer to [RGS] for general background on numerical semigroups. For positive integers a1,…,ana_{1},\dots,a_{n} with gcd⁡(a1,…,an)=1\gcd(a_{1},\dots,a_{n})=1, let

⟨a1,…,an⟩={λ1a1+⋯+λnan|λ1,…,λn∈ℤ≥0}\langle a_{1},\dots,a_{n}\rangle=\left\{\lambda_{1}a_{1}+\cdots+\lambda_{n}a_{n}\;\middle|\;\lambda_{1},\dots,\lambda_{n}\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\right\}

be the numerical semigroup generated by a1,…,ana_{1},\dots,a_{n}. Fix a field 𝕂\mathbb{K}. If H=⟨a1,…,an⟩H=\langle a_{1},\dots,a_{n}\rangle is minimally generated by a1,…,ana_{1},\dots,a_{n}, then the defining ideal IHI_{H} of the numerical semigroup ring 𝕂⁡[H]\mathbb{K}[H] is the kernel of the homomorphism

π:𝕂⁡[x1,…,xn]⟶𝕂⁡[H]=𝕂⁡[ta1,…,tan],π⁡(xi)=tai.\pi:\mathbb{K}[x_{1},\dots,x_{n}]\longrightarrow\mathbb{K}[H]=\mathbb{K}[t^{a_{1}},\dots,t^{a_{n}}],\qquad\pi(x_{i})=t^{a_{i}}.

Determining generators of the defining ideal of a numerical semigroup ring is a fundamental problem in the study of numerical semigroups; see, for example, [MS] for an overview of problems and recent developments. A classical result of Herzog [He] describes the defining ideals of numerical semigroups of embedding dimension three. In particular, if HH is generated by three elements and is not symmetric, then IHI_{H} is generated by the 2×22\times 2 minors of a 2×32\times 3 matrix. Recently, Cuong, Kien, Matsuoka, and Truong proposed the following conjectural characterization of higher-dimensional numerical semigroups with such a determinantal defining ideal; see [KMO, Conjecture 1.1]. Recall that an integer w∈ℤ≥0∖Hw\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\setminus H is called a pseudo-Frobenius number of HH if w+ai∈Hw+a_{i}\in H for every ii. We denote by PF⁡(H)\mathrm{PF}(H) the set of pseudo-Frobenius numbers of HH. For a matrix MM, we write I2​(M)I_{2}(M) for the ideal generated by its 22-minors.

Conjecture 1.1 (Cuong–Kien–Matsuoka–Truong).

Let n≥3n\geq 3, and let H=⟨a1,…,an⟩H=\langle a_{1},\dots,a_{n}\rangle be a numerical semigroup minimally generated by a1,…,ana_{1},\dots,a_{n}. Then the following conditions are equivalent.

  • (A)

    IHI_{H} is generated by the 2×22\times 2 minors of a 2×n2\times n whose entries are homogeneous elements of positive degree.

  • (B)

    There exist positive integers c1,…,cn,d1,…,dnc_{1},\dots,c_{n},d_{1},\dots,d_{n} such that

    (1.1) IH=I2​(x1c1⋯xn−1cn−1xncnx2d2⋯xndnx1d1).\displaystyle I_{H}=I_{2}\begin{pmatrix}x_{1}^{c_{1}}&\cdots&x_{n-1}^{c_{n-1}}&x_{n}^{c_{n}}\\ x_{2}^{d_{2}}&\cdots&x_{n}^{d_{n}}&x_{1}^{d_{1}}\end{pmatrix}.
  • (C)

    PF⁡(H)\mathrm{PF}(H) forms an arithmetic progression of length n−1n-1.

The implication (A)⇒(C)(A)\Rightarrow(C) was proved in [KM]; hence the open part of the conjecture is basically the implication (C)⇒(B)(C)\Rightarrow(B). The conjecture is known in several special cases, including almost symmetric numerical semigroups [GKMT], numerical semigroups whose embedding dimension is large relative to their multiplicity [KM, Ta], and stretched numerical semigroups [KMO]. Algebraic properties of numerical semigroup rings with determinantal defining ideals as in (1.1) have also studied in [KMN].

A difficulty in proving (C)⇒(B)(C)\Rightarrow(B) is that, even after suitable candidates for the exponents c1,…,cn,d1,…,dnc_{1},\dots,c_{n},d_{1},\dots,d_{n} have been identified, one still has to prove that the corresponding determinantal ideal is indeed the defining ideal IHI_{H}. Our first main result gives a numerical criterion that removes this difficulty.

To explain the result, let us recall a consequence of condition (B)(B). It was proved in [KM, Theorem 3] that, if (1.1) holds, then

PF⁡(H)={h+α,h+2​α,…,h+(n−1)​α},\mathrm{PF}(H)=\{h+\alpha,h+2\alpha,\dots,h+(n-1)\alpha\},

where

h=∑i=1n(ci−1)ai and α=di+1ai+1−ciai for all i,h=\sum_{i=1}^{n}(c_{i}-1)a_{i}\text{ and }\alpha=d_{i+1}a_{i+1}-c_{i}a_{i}\text{ for all $i$},

where we consider dn+1=d1d_{n+1}=d_{1} and an+1=a1a_{n+1}=a_{1}. Moreover, one obtains explicit numerical expressions of pseudo-Frobenius numbers in terms of the exponents cic_{i} and did_{i}:

(1.2) h+k​α=−(a1+⋯+an)+∑ℓ=2k+1dℓ​aℓ+∑ℓ=k+1ncℓ​aℓ\displaystyle h+k\alpha=-(a_{1}+\cdots+a_{n})+\sum_{\ell=2}^{k+1}d_{\ell}a_{\ell}+\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{n}c_{\ell}a_{\ell}

for k=0,1,2,…,nk=0,1,2,\dots,n. Thus condition (B)(B) imposes very explicit numerical identities on the pseudo-Frobenius numbers. A natural question is whether, conversely, these numerical identities are sufficient to recover the determinantal presentation of IHI_{H}. Our first main theorem shows that this is indeed the case.

Theorem 1.2.

Let H=⟨a1,…,an⟩H=\langle a_{1},\dots,a_{n}\rangle be a numerical semigroup minimally generated by a1,…,ana_{1},\dots,a_{n}, and assume that

PF⁡(H)={h+α,h+2​α,…,h+(n−1)​α}\mathrm{PF}(H)=\{h+\alpha,h+2\alpha,\dots,h+(n-1)\alpha\}

for some h,α∈ℤh,\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}, where α≠0\alpha\neq 0. Let c1,…,cn,d1,…,dnc_{1},\dots,c_{n},d_{1},\dots,d_{n} be positive integers. Then the following conditions are equivalent.

  • (1)

    IH=I2​(x1c1⋯xn−1cn−1xncnx2d2⋯xndnx1d1).I_{H}=I_{2}\begin{pmatrix}x_{1}^{c_{1}}&\cdots&x_{n-1}^{c_{n-1}}&x_{n}^{c_{n}}\\ x_{2}^{d_{2}}&\cdots&x_{n}^{d_{n}}&x_{1}^{d_{1}}\end{pmatrix}.

  • (2)

    The identities (1.2) hold for all k=0,1,2,…,nk=0,1,2,\dots,n.

The significance of Theorem 1.2 is that it separates the numerical-semigroup-theoretic part of Conjecture 1.1 from the commutative-algebraic verification of the defining ideal. In the proofs of the previously known cases of the conjecture [GKMT, KM, KMO, Ta], one first determines a candidate determinantal presentation and then proves separately that the resulting determinantal ideal coincides with IHI_{H}. Theorem 1.2 shows that the latter step follows automatically once the appropriate numerical identities for the pseudo-Frobenius numbers have been established.

In the second part of the paper, as an application of Theorem 1.2, we obtain a new partial affirmative result for Conjecture 1.1 in embedding dimension four. For w∈Hw\in H, we say that ww has a unique factorization in HH if there is a unique tuple (k1,…,kn)∈ℤ≥0n(k_{1},\dots,k_{n})\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^{n} such that w=k1​a1+⋯+kn​an.w=k_{1}a_{1}+\cdots+k_{n}a_{n}. For a nonzero element a∈Ha\in H, let

Ap⁡(H,a)={w∈H∣w−a∉H}\mathrm{Ap}(H,a)=\{w\in H\mid w-a\notin H\}

be the Apéry set of HH with respect to aa. We say that Ap⁡(H,a)\mathrm{Ap}(H,a) has unique factorizations in HH if every element of Ap⁡(H,a)\mathrm{Ap}(H,a) has a unique factorization in HH. Our second main result is the following.

Theorem 1.3.

Conjecture 1.1 holds when n=4n=4 and Ap⁡(H,ai)\mathrm{Ap}(H,a_{i}) has unique factorizations in HH for some ii.

At first sight, the assumption that Ap⁡(H,ai)\mathrm{Ap}(H,a_{i}) has unique factorizations may appear restrictive. However, among semigroups satisfying condition (B)(B), this condition is fairly mild in embedding dimension four. Indeed, as shown in Lemma 2.9, if

IH=I2​(x1c1x2c2x3c3x4c4x2d2x3d3x4d4x1d1),I_{H}=I_{2}\begin{pmatrix}x_{1}^{c_{1}}&x_{2}^{c_{2}}&x_{3}^{c_{3}}&x_{4}^{c_{4}}\\ x_{2}^{d_{2}}&x_{3}^{d_{3}}&x_{4}^{d_{4}}&x_{1}^{d_{1}}\end{pmatrix},

then Ap⁡(H,a1)\mathrm{Ap}(H,a_{1}) has unique factorizations if and only if

d2≤c2andc4≤d4.d_{2}\leq c_{2}\qquad\text{and}\qquad c_{4}\leq d_{4}.

Thus the failure of the unique-factorization condition is governed by simple inequalities among the exponents. In this sense, assuming Conjecture 1.1, Theorem 1.3 applies to a substantial part of the embedding-dimension-four case. We also note that, in the previously known cases of the conjecture [GKMT, KM, KMO, Ta], apart from Herzog’s classical three-generated case [He], at least half of the exponents c1,…,cn,d1,…,dnc_{1},\dots,c_{n},d_{1},\dots,d_{n} are equal to 11. Our result does not require such a restriction.

This paper is organized as follows. In Section 2, we recall some basic facts on numerical semigroups, Apéry sets, and Gröbner bases. In Section 3, we establish Theorem 1.2, our numerical criterion for determinantal presentations. In Section 4, we study the embedding-dimension-four case and prove Theorem 1.3. We conclude with some remarks and examples.

2. Preliminary

In this section, we recall some basic facts about Apéry sets, pseudo-Frobenius numbers, numerical semigroup rings, and Gröbner bases.

Throughout the paper for integer vectors v=(v1,…,vt),u=(u1,…,ut)v=(v_{1},\dots,v_{t}),u=(u_{1},\dots,u_{t}) we write v≥uv\geq u if vi≥uiv_{i}\geq u_{i} for all ii. Let ≤H\leq_{H} be the partial order on ℤ\mathbb{Z} defined by a≤Hba\leq_{H}b if b−a∈Hb-a\in H. We recall the following standard properties of Apéry sets; see [RGS, Lemma 2.4 and Proposition 2.20].

Lemma 2.1.

Let H=⟨a1,…,an⟩H=\langle a_{1},\dots,a_{n}\rangle be the numerical semigroup minimally generated by a1,…,ana_{1},\dots,a_{n}, and let 0≠a∈H0\neq a\in H. Then the following statements hold.

  1. (1)

    a+PF⁡(H)={a+p∣p∈PF⁡(H)}a+\mathrm{PF}(H)=\{a+p\mid p\in\mathrm{PF}(H)\} is exactly the set of maximal elements of Ap⁡(H,a)\mathrm{Ap}(H,a) with respect to the partial order ≤H\leq_{H}.

  2. (2)

    For each i=0,1,…,a−1i=0,1,\dots,a-1, there is a unique element w∈Ap⁡(H,a)w\in\mathrm{Ap}(H,a) such that w≡i(moda)w\equiv i\pmod{a}.

  3. (3)

    If w∈Ap⁡(H,a)w\in\mathrm{Ap}(H,a) and u≤Hwu\leq_{H}w, then u∈Ap⁡(H,a)u\in\mathrm{Ap}(H,a).

We next recall the algebraic interpretations of Apéry sets and pseudo-Frobenius numbers. Let H=⟨a1,…,an⟩H=\langle a_{1},\dots,a_{n}\rangle be a numerical semigroup minimally generated by a1,…,ana_{1},\dots,a_{n}, and let S=𝕂⁡[x1,…,xn]S=\mathbb{K}[x_{1},\dots,x_{n}] be the polynomial ring with grading deg⁡xi=ai\deg x_{i}=a_{i} for all ii. The numerical semigroup ring of HH over 𝕂\mathbb{K} is

𝕂⁡[H]=𝕂⁡[ta1,…,tan]⊆𝕂⁡[t].\mathbb{K}[H]=\mathbb{K}[t^{a_{1}},\dots,t^{a_{n}}]\subseteq\mathbb{K}[t].

Its defining ideal IH⊆SI_{H}\subseteq S is the kernel of the graded homomorphism

π:S⟶𝕂⁡[H]\pi:S\longrightarrow\mathbb{K}[H]

defined by π⁡(xi)=tai\pi(x_{i})=t^{a_{i}} for all ii. The following statement follows directly from the definition of an Apéry set.

Lemma 2.2.

With the notation above, x1k1⋯xnknx_{1}^{k_{1}}\cdots x_{n}^{k_{n}} is nonzero in S/(IH+(xi))S/(I_{H}+(x_{i})) if and only f w=k1​a1+⋯+kn​an∈Hw=k_{1}a_{1}+\cdots+k_{n}a_{n}\in H belongs to Ap⁡(H,ai)\mathrm{Ap}(H,a_{i}).

We also need the following fact.

Lemma 2.3 (see [KMO, Proposition 2.10]).

Let H=⟨a1,…,an⟩H=\langle a_{1},\dots,a_{n}\rangle be a numerical semigroup generated by a1,…,ana_{1},\dots,a_{n}. Let JJ be a graded ideal of SS such that J⊆IHJ\subseteq I_{H}. If J+(x1)=IH+(x1)J+(x_{1})=I_{H}+(x_{1}), then J=IHJ=I_{H}.

We now recall the relation between pseudo-Frobenius numbers and socles. For a graded 𝕂\mathbb{K}-algebra AA with its graded maximal ideal 𝔪A\mathfrak{m}_{A}, its socle is

socle⁡(A)={f∈A∣𝔪A​f=0}.\mathrm{socle}(A)=\{f\in A\mid\mathfrak{m}_{A}f=0\}.

We will also use the following elementary observation.

Lemma 2.4.

Let II be a graded ideal of SS such that dim𝕂(S/I)<∞\dim_{\mathbb{K}}(S/I)<\infty. For every nonzero element ff of S/IS/I, there is an element m∈Sm\in S such that 0≠m​f∈socle⁡(S/I)0\neq mf\in\mathrm{socle}(S/I).

Socles are closely related to pseudo-Frobenius numbers. The following result may be viewed as an algebraic analogue of Lemma 2.1(1).

Lemma 2.5 (see [HMR, §5.1.1]).

With the notation above, the set

{tw∣w∈ai+PF⁡(H)}\{t^{w}\mid w\in a_{i}+\mathrm{PF}(H)\}

forms a 𝕂\mathbb{K}-basis of socle⁡(𝕂⁡[H]/(tai))\mathrm{socle}(\mathbb{K}[H]/(t^{a_{i}})).

We next recall some basic facts about Gröbner bases. We refer the reader to [Ei, §15] and [HH, Chapter 2] for the basic theory of Gröbner bases. Let >rev>_{\mathrm{rev}} be the weighted graded reverse lexicographic order on SS with x1<⋯<xnx_{1}<\cdots<x_{n}. Thus, for monomials u=x1k1⋯xnknu=x_{1}^{k_{1}}\cdots x_{n}^{k_{n}} and v=x1ℓ1⋯xnℓnv=x_{1}^{\ell_{1}}\cdots x_{n}^{\ell_{n}}, one has u>revvu>_{\mathrm{rev}}v if and only if

  1. (i)

    deg⁡u>deg⁡v\deg u>\deg v, or

  2. (ii)

    deg⁡u=deg⁡v\deg u=\deg v and the leftmost nonzero entry of (ℓ1−k1,…,ℓn−kn)(\ell_{1}-k_{1},\dots,\ell_{n}-k_{n}) is positive.

Here the grading on SS is given by deg⁡xi=ai\deg x_{i}=a_{i}. For a polynomial 0≠f∈S0\neq f\in S and an ideal I⊂SI\subset S, we write in(f)\mathop{\mathrm{in}}(f) and in(I)\mathop{\mathrm{in}}(I) for the initial monomial of ff and the initial ideal of II with respect to >rev>_{\mathrm{rev}}, respectively. A subset 𝒢⊂I\mathcal{G}\subset I is called a Gröbner basis of II if

in(I)=(in(f)∣f∈𝒢).\mathop{\mathrm{in}}(I)=(\mathop{\mathrm{in}}(f)\mid f\in\mathcal{G}).
Lemma 2.6 (see [Ei, Proposition 15.12]).

For any graded ideal II of SS, one has

in(I+(x1))=in(I)+(x1).\mathop{\mathrm{in}}(I+(x_{1}))=\mathop{\mathrm{in}}(I)+(x_{1}).

For a monomial ideal II of SS, we write ℳ⁡(I)\mathcal{M}(I) for the set of monomials in SS that are not contained in II.

Lemma 2.7 (see [HH, Proposition 2.2.5]).

For any ideal II of SS, the set ℳ⁡(in(I))\mathcal{M}(\mathop{\mathrm{in}}(I)) forms an 𝕂\mathbb{K}-basis of S/IS/I.

We will also use the following inequality comparing the socles of S/IS/I and S/in(I)S/\mathop{\mathrm{in}}(I).

Lemma 2.8 (see [HH, Theorem 3.3.1]).

For any graded ideal II of SS, one has

dim𝕂(socle⁡(S/I))≤dim𝕂(socle⁡(S/in(I))).\dim_{\mathbb{K}}\big(\mathrm{socle}(S/I)\big)\leq\dim_{\mathbb{K}}\big(\mathrm{socle}(S/\mathop{\mathrm{in}}(I))\big).

We finally discuss when Ap⁡(H,a1)\mathrm{Ap}(H,a_{1}) has unique factorizations in HH in the case where IHI_{H} has the determinantal presentation (1.1). Assume that H=⟨a1,a2,a3,a4⟩H=\langle a_{1},a_{2},a_{3},a_{4}\rangle is the numerical semigroup minimally generated by a1,…,a4a_{1},\dots,a_{4} and

IH=I2​(x1c1x2c2x3c3x4c4x2d2x3d3x4d4x1d1).I_{H}=I_{2}\begin{pmatrix}x_{1}^{c_{1}}&x_{2}^{c_{2}}&x_{3}^{c_{3}}&x_{4}^{c_{4}}\\ x_{2}^{d_{2}}&x_{3}^{d_{3}}&x_{4}^{d_{4}}&x_{1}^{d_{1}}\end{pmatrix}.

As follows from (1.2), we have

PF⁡(H)={p1=h+α,p2=h+2​α,p3=h+3​α},\mathrm{PF}(H)=\{p_{1}=h+\alpha,p_{2}=h+2\alpha,p_{3}=h+3\alpha\},

where

p1=h+α=−a1+(c2+d2−1)​a2+(c3−1)​a3+(c4−1)​a4,p2=h+2​α=−a1+(d2−1)​a2+(c3+d3−1)​a3+(c4−1)​a4,p3=h+3​α=−a1+(d2−1)​a2+(d3−1)​a3+(c4+d4−1)​a4.\displaystyle\begin{array}[]{ll}p_{1}&=h+\alpha=-a_{1}+(c_{2}+d_{2}-1)a_{2}+(c_{3}-1)a_{3}+(c_{4}-1)a_{4},\\ p_{2}&=h+2\alpha=-a_{1}+(d_{2}-1)a_{2}+(c_{3}+d_{3}-1)a_{3}+(c_{4}-1)a_{4},\\ p_{3}&=h+3\alpha=-a_{1}+(d_{2}-1)a_{2}+(d_{3}-1)a_{3}+(c_{4}+d_{4}-1)a_{4}.\end{array}
Lemma 2.9.

With the same notation as above, one has

  1. (1)

    a1+p1a_{1}+p_{1} has a unique factorization in HH if and only if c4≤d4c_{4}\leq d_{4}.

  2. (2)

    a1+p2a_{1}+p_{2} has a unique factorization in HH if and only if c4≤d4c_{4}\leq d_{4} or d2≤c2d_{2}\leq c_{2}.

  3. (3)

    a1+p3a_{1}+p_{3} has a unique factorization in HH if and only if d2≤c2d_{2}\leq c_{2}.

In particular, Ap⁡(H,a1)\mathrm{Ap}(H,a_{1}) has unique factorizations in HH if and only if c4≤d4c_{4}\leq d_{4} and d2≤c2d_{2}\leq c_{2}.

Proof.

Recall that an element w∈Hw\in H belongs to Ap⁡(H,a1)\mathrm{Ap}(H,a_{1}) if and only if it has no factorization of the form w=k1​a1+k2​a2+k3​a3+k4​a4w=k_{1}a_{1}+k_{2}a_{2}+k_{3}a_{3}+k_{4}a_{4} with k1,…,k4∈ℤ≥0k_{1},\dots,k_{4}\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0} and k1>0k_{1}>0. Modulo (x1)(x_{1}), the only generator of IH+(x1)I_{H}+(x_{1}) that can identify two nonzero monomials is

x3c3+d3−x2c2​x4d4.x_{3}^{c_{3}+d_{3}}-x_{2}^{c_{2}}x_{4}^{d_{4}}.

Indeed, all the other 2×22\times 2 minors reduce modulo (x1)(x_{1}) to monomials, which vanish in S/(IH+(x1))S/(I_{H}+(x_{1})). Hence, if

w=k2​a2+k3​a3+k4​a4∈Ap⁡(H,a1),w=k_{2}a_{2}+k_{3}a_{3}+k_{4}a_{4}\in\mathrm{Ap}(H,a_{1}),

then the monomial x2k2​x3k3​x4k4x_{2}^{k_{2}}x_{3}^{k_{3}}x_{4}^{k_{4}} admits another monomial representative of the same HH-degree if and only if it is divisible by either x3c3+d3x_{3}^{c_{3}+d_{3}} or x2c2​x4d4x_{2}^{c_{2}}x_{4}^{d_{4}}. Equivalently, ww has more than one factorization in HH if and only if k3≥c3+d3k_{3}\geq c_{3}+d_{3} or (k2,k4)≥(c2,d4)(k_{2},k_{4})\geq(c_{2},d_{4}). Applying this criterion to (2), we obtain statements (1)–(3).

Finally, Ap⁡(H,a1)\mathrm{Ap}(H,a_{1}) has unique factorizations in HH if and only if its maximal elements a1+p1,a1+p2,a1+p3a_{1}+p_{1},a_{1}+p_{2},a_{1}+p_{3} have unique factorizations in HH. Indeed, if w≤Hvw\leq_{H}v and ww has two distinct factorizations, then any factorization of v−wv-w extends them to two distinct factorizations of vv. ∎

3. Proof of Theorem 1.2

In this section, after establishing a few preliminary lemmas, we prove our first main theorem. Throughout this section, let H=⟨a1,…,an⟩H=\langle a_{1},\dots,a_{n}\rangle be a numerical semigroup minimally generated by a1,…,ana_{1},\dots,a_{n}, and let S=𝕂⁡[x1,…,xn]S=\mathbb{K}[x_{1},\dots,x_{n}] with deg⁡xi=ai\deg x_{i}=a_{i}. We also fix positive integers c1,…,cn,d1,…,dnc_{1},\dots,c_{n},d_{1},\dots,d_{n} and write

J=I2​(x1c1⋯xn−1cn−1xncnx2d2⋯xndnx1d1).J=I_{2}\begin{pmatrix}x_{1}^{c_{1}}&\cdots&x_{n-1}^{c_{n-1}}&x_{n}^{c_{n}}\\ x_{2}^{d_{2}}&\cdots&x_{n}^{d_{n}}&x_{1}^{d_{1}}\end{pmatrix}.

To simplify notation, we set xn+1=x1x_{n+1}=x_{1}, cn+1=c1c_{n+1}=c_{1}, and dn+1=d1d_{n+1}=d_{1}. We note that JJ is homogeneous with respect to the grading deg⁡xi=ai\deg x_{i}=a_{i} if and only if ci​ai−di+1​ai+1c_{i}a_{i}-d_{i+1}a_{i+1} is independent of ii.

Lemma 3.1.

If JJ is a graded ideal of SS, then the set

𝒢={xi+1di+1​xjcj−xici​xj+1dj+1∣1≤i<j≤n}\mathcal{G}=\{x_{i+1}^{d_{i+1}}x_{j}^{c_{j}}-x_{i}^{c_{i}}x_{j+1}^{d_{j+1}}\mid 1\leq i<j\leq n\}

is a Gröbner basis of JJ with respect to >rev>_{\mathrm{rev}}.

Proof.

We use Buchberger’s criterion (see [HH, Theorem 2.3.2]). We write f→𝑔hf\xrightarrow{g}h if hh is obtained from ff by a single polynomial reduction using gg, and f→𝒢hf\xrightarrow{\mathcal{G}}h if ff reduces to hh by a finite sequence of polynomial reductions using elements of 𝒢\mathcal{G}. For 1≤i<j≤n1\leq i<j\leq n, let

fi,j=xi+1di+1​xjcj−xici​xj+1dj+1.f_{i,j}=x_{i+1}^{d_{i+1}}x_{j}^{c_{j}}-x_{i}^{c_{i}}x_{j+1}^{d_{j+1}}.

Thus 𝒢={fi,j∣1≤i<j≤n}\mathcal{G}=\{f_{i,j}\mid 1\leq i<j\leq n\}. It suffices to prove that

S⁡(fi,j,fk,ℓ)⟶𝒢0S(f_{i,j},f_{k,\ell})\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathcal{G}}}{{\longrightarrow}}0

Remark 4.4.

Numerical semigroups having an Apéry set of unique expression were studied by Rosales [Ros]. In particular, it was shown in [Ros] that, under this assumption, a minimal presentation of the numerical semigroup can be described in terms of the minimal elements lying outside the Apéry set. Our proof of Theorem 1.3 first obtains explicit presentations of the maximal elements of Ap⁡(H,a1)\mathrm{Ap}(H,a_{1}) and then uses these presentations to control the defining ideal. Rosales’ result appears to be closely related to the second step of our proof, although we have not investigated whether it can be applied directly in our setting.

Final remark and examples

Although Ap⁡(H,ai)\mathrm{Ap}(H,a_{i}) does not always have a unique factorization, we still think that the approach of this paper is useful to study Conjecture 1.1 at least for the case when n=4n=4. For example, Lemma 2.9 suggests that if the conjecture holds then by an appropriate choice of ii one should have (i) ai+p1a_{i}+p_{1} and ai+p2a_{i}+p_{2} have the unique factorizations in HH, or (ii) ai+p2a_{i}+p_{2} and ai+p3a_{i}+p_{3} have the unique factorizations in HH. If one can prove such a uniqueness statement only assuming that PF⁡(H)\mathrm{PF}(H) forms an arithmetic progression of length 33, some of the argument in this paper will be applicable to attach the n=4n=4 case of the conjecture.

We conclude the paper with two examples of four-generated numerical semigroups whose pseudo-Frobenius numbers form an arithmetic progression, one for which the Apéry set has unique factorizations and one for which it does not.

Example 4.5.

Let H=⟨a1=17,a2=40,a3=42,a4=45⟩H=\langle a_{1}=17,a_{2}=40,a_{3}=42,a_{4}=45\rangle. Then PF⁡(H)={145,151,157}\mathrm{PF}(H)=\{145,151,157\} with h=139h=139 and α=6\alpha=6. Thus, we have

IH=I2​(X12X23X32X4X2X33X42X13).I_{H}=\mathrm{I}_{2}\left(\begin{matrix}X_{1}^{2}&X_{2}^{3}&X_{3}^{2}&X_{4}\\ X_{2}&X_{3}^{3}&X_{4}^{2}&X_{1}^{3}\end{matrix}\right).

Since 1=d2≤c2=31=d_{2}\leq c_{2}=3 and 2=d4≥c4=12=d_{4}\geq c_{4}=1, by Lemma 2.9, this Apéry set has unique factorizations in HH.

Example 4.6.

Let H=⟨a1=7,a2=15,a3=16,a4=17⟩H=\langle a_{1}=7,a_{2}=15,a_{3}=16,a_{4}=17\rangle. Then PF⁡(H)={25,26,27}\mathrm{PF}(H)=\{25,26,27\} with h=24h=24 and α=1\alpha=1. We have

IH=I2​(X12X2X3X42X2X3X4X15).I_{H}=I_{2}\left(\begin{matrix}X_{1}^{2}&X_{2}&X_{3}&X_{4}^{2}\\ X_{2}&X_{3}&X_{4}&X_{1}^{5}\end{matrix}\right).

The element 3232 of Ap\mathrm{Ap} has the following two factorizations,

32=a2+a4=2​a3.32=a_{2}+a_{4}=2a_{3}.

Thus, this Apéry set does not have unique factorizations in HH.
